term: finite origin-code admissibility along an indexed channel
definition: If station n outputs a numeric code j, then n<=j. Upstream stations have increasing natural-number indices; a code names its own or a strictly earlier station. This property constrains every output, not only one observed downstream output.
note: A finite code bound is separate from merely labeling a token. PGR's indexed positions suggest this candidate interpretation subject to correct detection and maintenance; the later active/passive signal description alone does not explicitly enforce numeric validation. It is not well-foundedness of the successor channel, which has infinite upstream chains. Metaphysical realization and causal interpretation remain OPEN.
